correctness.rationale: The Perrin sequence is the trace sequence of an integral unimodular companion matrix, so the classical prime-power matrix Gauss congruence applies to both positive and negative indices. This yields exponent descent. Exact modular checks by two independent algebraic representations verify the lift failures used in the finite classification.

originality.rationale: The matrix Gauss congruence and the A173656 square condition are prior results and are not claimed as new. Searches did not locate the Perrin-specific prime-power descent formulation, the two-sided square-lift criterion, or the resulting classification below 10^20. Originality is to the best of our knowledge, with material residual risk from older recurrence-pseudoprime literature whose complete text was not directly inspected.

value.rationale: The result organizes prime-power Perrin pseudoprimes into initial exponent segments, converts square-lift data into a general search reduction, and gives an exact database-assisted frontier below 10^20 for unrestricted and restricted variants.
